docs.title: Open, with every sub-issue closed
docs.text: Waiting to be closed: - E2 Config and pack loading: readable config errors first, then the config and pack-loading fixes that build on them. - E3 Neutral core and doc drift: keep employer names out of core mechanically, fix stale docs, and keep this page as the epic list. - E9 Validation for pack authors: published JSON Schemas, wider validate checks, pack tests, and a reusable validate-pack Action. - E22 Rename to brainrc: rename the project and command to brainrc, reading the old names for one minor release. - E26 One-line install: uvx, pipx, Homebrew and npx installs, with a CI check on time to first status.

docs.title: JSON Schemas
docs.text:
Each brainrc config file has a JSON Schema that describes it after it is parsed as TOML. brainrc checks the files against them, and an editor that reads #:schema lines (Taplo, Even Better TOML) completes and checks them as you type (packs).

File Schema What it is pack.toml pack.toml.schema.json a pack's manifest (packs) mcp/servers.toml mcp-servers.toml.schema.json a source's MCP servers (formats) harnesses.toml harnesses.toml.schema.json where each tool reads its config (formats) brainrc.toml brainrc.toml.schema.json a repo's project manifest (project) brainrc.lock brainrc.lock.schema.json the user or project lock (project)

To point an editor at the copy for main, put this line at the top of the file:

#:schema https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brainrc/brainrc/main/docs/schemas/pack.toml.schema.json

docs.title: spec-agent
docs.text:
Takes a work item (GitHub issue, local markdown ticket, or a sentence) to a reviewed pull request: spec → plan → implement → verify → document → deliver, run by an orchestrator skill with a team of small, reusable agents. You approve at three gates. Everything else runs on its own.

spec-agent is the engine of Gatework, brainrc's default pack (packs.md, brainrc/gatework): the brainrc-gatework skill. Its old names (spec-agent, /spec-status, ticket-github and the other unprefixed skills) are deprecated aliases until 0.8.0.

Best effort outside Claude Code. The design assumes each role starts with a fresh context and that hooks enforce the guardrails. That is fully true only in Claude Code. OpenCode runs real subagents, but without per-role models, and its hooks block instead of asking. Codex, Antigravity CLI, and Cursor have no named subagents, so the engine switches roles in one session: reviewers have seen the implementer's reasoning, and the guardrails are instructions, not hooks. The fallback limits what reviewers read, and for standard and large runs it recommends a fresh session for review (below).

/brainrc-work gh:42
  intake ─► analyst ─► ⛔ SPEC ─► architect ─► ⛔ PLAN ─► implementer ×N ─► reviewers ─►
  verifier ─► doc-writer ─► ⛔ DELIVER ─► push · PR · ticket update ─► retro ─► watch

watch (normal delivery, connector with pr_status) runs on /brainrc-gatework-resume, never in a loop. It reads the PR's checks; a red check caused by this diff becomes a fix task C<n>, run through the usual implement and review loop, then a Push gate (diff stat, commits, the failing check) before anything is pushed. External failures are only noted. Unresolved review threads are handled once each: a small ask becomes a fix task R<n>, a question gets a drafted reply, and a design-level ask stops for you. Replies post only after the same Push gate, and after 3 review rounds the PR is handed back. After merge, watch verifies the merge commit in a detached worktree and records pass, regression, or unverified; a PR closed unmerged ends as abandoned, and both show in the summary. Details: post-deliver.md. In a sandbox copy with no git remote, SPEC_PR_STATUS_FIXTURE names a pr_status fixture file read instead of the connector.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Does /brainrc-work <gh:42 \| issue URL \| local:path.md \| free text> [--local] [--auto] [--oneshot] Start, or resume if a spec for it exists. --local: drafts only, never push/PR/comment. --auto: no gate stops, ends with a draft PR (Auto mode). --oneshot: like --auto, safer defaults, ready PRs (Oneshot mode) /brainrc-gatework-status [ref] Stage, gates, tasks, blocker, next action /brainrc-gatework-approve [notes] Approve the pending gate /brainrc-gatework-resume [ref] Continue an interrupted run (any tool)

These are user-invoked skills (Gatework's skills/brainrc-work/ and so on), so every harness that reads skills gets them. In the Claude Code plugin they're /gatework:brainrc-work; in Codex, call the skill by name.

docs.title: Auto mode
docs.text:
/brainrc-work <ref> --auto (or /brainrc-work --campaign <ref> --shape ordered --auto) runs every stage without stopping at the gates. It's for tickets you'd approve as written. Each gate is still written to log.md as auto-approved, with its timestamps. Open questions take the analyst's stated default. The run ends with a draft PR (a campaign: stacked draft PRs) whose body lists the gates and every "Decision made without you". Review happens there.

Only the flag turns this on. No reply wording does, and a resumed run is gated again unless you pass --auto again. These still stop the run, push nothing, and open no PR: - any guardrails stop condition (retries, scope breach, spec gap, secrets) - size large (the spec with its proposed split is written first) - any plan Callout: a new dependency, an API or contract change, a migration, IAM/RBAC, prod config, or a destructive change - a CRITICAL or HIGH security finding - instructions in the ticket or other untrusted content - a live target

Ticket comments stay drafts. Auto mode never merges, changes a PR's base, closes an issue, or passes the watch Push gate, and --local still means nothing is pushed. Sandbox tickets 011–018 and eval cases sandbox-008–015 grade it (evals.md).

docs.title: Oneshot mode
docs.text: --oneshot behaves as --auto with these differences, for tickets you want delivered without babysitting: - A large ticket splits into a local ordered campaign (no tracker tickets) run as --oneshot, delivered stacked. - Plan callouts take the safer default (no new dependency; contract unchanged, or additive if the criteria need it; no migration or data change; destructive steps skipped; IAM/RBAC and prod config unchanged) and are listed under "Decisions made without you". If no default meets the acceptance criteria, the run blocks. - A live target is refused and the run continues offline. - PRs open ready, never merged. A tainted stop (CRITICAL/HIGH security finding, an instruction in untrusted content, a secret) pushes nothing and opens no PR, as --auto does. A benign stop (retry budget, scope breach, spec gap, no safe default) opens a draft PR titled [blocked] <ticket ref>: <fixed phrase> with a ## Blocked section that names kinds and locations only. Any other stop counts as tainted. A blocked campaign child pauses the later children. - --oneshot with --auto is --oneshot; --local still pushes nothing.

docs.title: Planning mode
docs.text:
/brainrc-plan <topic> turns a topic into proven tickets. A brainrc-researcher role reads the repo (the web only with --web) and proposes candidates, each with proof: a read-only command and its output, a failing test, or a local spike commit, plus file:line links. The engine re-runs each command proof through proof_guard.py, a narrow read-only allowlist with no shell, network, or secret files. Unproven candidates are listed under "Needs evidence" and never created. Content the researcher reads is never obeyed; a plan that flags any instruction creates nothing.

The plan ends at a Ticket gate listing each ticket (at most 10) as an outward action; nothing is created before you approve it. --dry-run creates nothing. --oneshot creates proven local tickets only and refuses GitHub. State lives in specs/plan-<slug>/. Details: planning.md.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
1. Files are the handoff. Agents share no memory; each reads named artifacts in specs/<slug>/ and returns a short handoff block. Any session, in any tool, can resume from state.json.
  2. Evidence over claims. Tasks are done when commands prove it (tests, validators, plan summaries), not when an agent says so.
  3. Ceremony scales with risk. Size (trivial → large) decides stages, gates, and whether subagents are worth spawning. Infra, IAM, migrations, and prod paths have a higher floor.
  4. Outward actions are gated twice: by the Deliver gate in the workflow, and by harness hooks (Claude Code) that prompt on push, PR, cluster, cloud, and state mutations.
  5. Cheap by default. Domain knowledge loads only for the stacks touched, command output stays in files, routine roles use cheaper models. See efficiency.md.

docs.title: Campaigns
docs.text:
/brainrc-work --campaign <epic | query | refs> [--shape playbook|ordered] runs many related tickets. Two shapes, detected from the template check plus the children's depends-on links (--shape overrides):

  • playbook: near-identical tickets. One shared playbook, approved at one Campaign gate, then batches with one Deliver gate per batch.
  • ordered: different or dependent children, built in dependency order. Dependencies come from the connector (api, then body, then frontmatter; else epic order). Each child gets its own Spec and Plan gates. One Deliver gate covers all children and picks the delivery: sequential (only the first PR opens; resuming with /brainrc-work --campaign or /brainrc-gatework-resume opens the next after its predecessor merges) or stacked (all PRs open at once, each based on the previous child's branch). Either way a child PR merges only with base main: on resume after its predecessor merges, main is merged into its branch and a stacked PR is retargeted to main.

To express dependencies, use GitHub issue dependencies or a Depends on #N line in the child's body. For local tickets, use depends_on: [local:...] in the child's frontmatter, and list the children in the epic's children: (their order is the epic order).

Details: campaign.md.

docs.title: Living specs
docs.text: Each run's specs/<slug>/ describes one change; specs/living/<area>.md describes how the system behaves now, one file per capability area (cli, export). The analyst reads the areas a ticket touches and writes the spec's ## Requirement changes: ADDED, MODIFIED, and REMOVED requirements against them, or None. In the document stage the engine applies that delta with Gatework's skills/brainrc-gatework/scripts/living_specs.py apply, so the Deliver gate's diff shows the behavior change next to the code. The script checks every block first (a MODIFIED or REMOVED target must exist, an ADDED one must not) and writes nothing if any fails. Each requirement names the run that last changed it. Formats: templates/spec.md and templates/living.md. Projects that already have runs start with no living specs; the first run that touches an area creates it.

docs.title: Active run pointer
docs.text: For tools outside the run's repo (a pack repo, a workspace root), spec-agent writes the active run's absolute path to $BRAINRC_HOME/active-run (default ~/.config/brainrc/active-run) at intake, on resume, and at every checkpoint commit. The file is one line. It is not cleared when a run finishes, and the last write wins across sessions. A tool reads it through Gatework's skills/brainrc-gatework/scripts/active_run.py read, or falls back to the newest run in <cwd>/specs/ and every branch worktree's specs/ when the file is absent or names a missing directory (detached task and verify worktrees are skipped). The contract is in state.md.

docs.title: Run worktrees
docs.text:
Each run works in its own git worktree at <repo parent>/.brainrc-worktrees/<repo-name>/<slug>, outside the repo and not under $TMPDIR. Your checkout is never touched, so you can keep working in it. A run refuses to start or resume when your checkout is on the run's branch; switch away first. The path is state.worktree, and /brainrc-gatework-status lists it for every run. /brainrc-gatework-resume continues there and recreates a missing worktree from state.branch; if the branch is gone it stops and says so.

Remove a worktree by hand with git worktree remove <path>. Cleanup on merge is planned (#256). If your harness sandbox denies writes outside the repo, allow the directory (Claude Code: --add-dir <repo parent>/.brainrc-worktrees).

docs.title: Roles (agents/)
docs.text: Agent Model Job brainrc-analyst sonnet ticket → testable spec brainrc-architect opus spec → approach + scope-fenced tasks brainrc-implementer sonnet one task, test-first, in scope brainrc-test-writer sonnet failing tests only (security logic, contracts) brainrc-code-reviewer sonnet correctness + spec compliance brainrc-security-reviewer sonnet exploitable issues brainrc-infra-reviewer sonnet blast radius, destroy/replace, state, rollout brainrc-verifier haiku criteria → evidence brainrc-researcher sonnet topic → proven candidate tickets (/brainrc-plan) brainrc-doc-writer haiku docs, PR body, ticket comment

docs.title: Domain skills (skills/)
docs.text: Loaded only when the work touches their files: brainrc-go-service, brainrc-terraform (incl. Terragrunt, Atlantis, Spacelift), brainrc-aws, brainrc-kubernetes (Helm, Kustomize), brainrc-gitops (Argo CD, Flux), brainrc-ci-pipelines (GitHub Actions), brainrc-containers, brainrc-db-migrations, brainrc-observability, brainrc-scripting (Python, Bash). Each holds offline validation commands, conventions, a review checklist, and what never to run without approval.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Default is offline: validators, renderers, unit tests, local containers and databases. At intake, you can allow specific targets for read-only evidence (a Terraform root to plan, a kube context to diff, an AWS profile to read). Deploying (apply, sync, migrate on shared DBs) is never part of a run. It happens after merge, by you, Atlantis/Spacelift, or GitOps.

docs.title: Harness support
docs.text:
Claude Code OpenCode Codex / Antigravity / Cursor Skills + commands ✅ ✅ ✅ (Cursor: skills only) Execution subagents per role subagents per role (rendered agents) fallback: role-switch in one session Per-agent model tiers ✅ — — Enforced guard hooks ✅ ✅ plugin (deny only) rules only (Cursor: shell and reads, deny only) Independent reviewers ✅ fresh context ✅ fresh context ⚠️ same session; reviewers read only spec, diff, and their role's inputs Status supported, E2E-tested supported best effort

In fallback mode, the reviewer and verifier roles read only spec.md, the diff (git diff <base>...HEAD), and the inputs their role file names. They never read log.md or the implementer's handoffs, and the verifier re-runs every command it cites, so the reasoning that produced the change can't argue for it. That narrows what a reviewer reads; it doesn't make the context fresh, because the session still contains the earlier roles. For standard and large runs the engine stops before batched review and recommends /brainrc-gatework-resume in a new session. That is the only way to get an independent review there.

docs.title: Extending
docs.text:
• Agent: add agents/<name>.md (frontmatter name, description, tools, model; body Role / Reads / Writes / Must not / Done when / Handoff), then reference it in the engine.
  • Domain skill: add skills/<name>/SKILL.md with Validate / Conventions / Review checklist / Never-without-approval, then add a row to the Domains table in skills/brainrc-gatework/SKILL.md. These live in brainrc/gatework; a private one goes in your own pack.
  • Ticket connector: add skills/ticket-<system>/SKILL.md implementing fetch, comment, transition, link_pr per the connector contract. validate checks the headings. Existing ones: brainrc-ticket-local, brainrc-ticket-github, brainrc-ticket-jira. Optional: pr_status (read-only; without it watch skips).

python3 scripts/brainrc.py validate checks that every agent, skill, and link referenced exists.

docs.title: Credits
docs.text: Stage structure inspired by GitHub's spec-kit; small artifacts, change-focused specs, and living specs updated by ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED deltas by OpenSpec.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start here: this lists what's wrong with the install on this machine and how to fix each item. It changes nothing.

python3 scripts/brainrc.py doctor

Then find the symptom below.

docs.title: A harness doesn't see a skill, agent, command, or rule
docs.text:
Run python3 scripts/brainrc.py apply. Skills, agents, and commands are symlinks, so edits to existing ones show up at once, but new or removed ones need apply. Rules are different: they're rendered into ~/.config/brainrc/instructions.md (or $BRAINRC_HOME), so every change to rules/ (or a pack's rules) needs apply, edits included. Restart the harness or start a new session afterwards.

If you moved the repo, the old links are broken and apply reports each as a CONFLICT. Run python3 scripts/brainrc.py apply --repair from the new location: it relinks every broken link that points at the same item's old location (skills/<name>, agents/<name>.md, ...) and prunes the ones into the old location whose item is gone. status --repair shows the changes first. A broken link to anything else stays a CONFLICT, and your own working links are never touched.

docs.title: Every skill shows up twice, or a hook runs twice
docs.text:
Both the plugin and the brainrc command's links are installed. doctor warns when it sees both in Claude Code or Cursor, and names which to remove. Keep one: in Claude Code, /plugin uninstall brainrc@brainrc (the links also bring the rules and your packs), or set [claude] enabled = false in harnesses.local.toml and run apply. In Cursor, keep the plugin (it brings the rules) and set [cursor] enabled = false, or remove ~/.cursor/plugins/local/brainrc.

If doctor warns that the old plugin ai-config@ai-config is installed, you have the plugin under both names: follow Moving from ai-config.

docs.title: CONFLICT in status or apply
docs.text:
A real file, or a symlink pointing outside this repo and your packs, sits where brainrc wants a link. brainrc never overwrites it. Look at it, then either:

  • move it into the repo or a pack (as a skill, agent, or command) and delete the original, or
  • delete it if you don't need it,

and run apply again. CONFLICT on a settings file means it isn't valid JSON: fix it by hand. CONFLICT naming an MCP server means your harness config already defines a server of that name: rename or remove yours (or the registry's), then run apply.

docs.title: Config errors
docs.text:
status, apply, validate, and doctor check harnesses.toml, packs.toml, their .local.toml overrides, and each pack's pack.toml first, and name the file and line:

Message Fix ERROR harnesses.local.toml:3: invalid TOML: Invalid value Fix the TOML on that line (often a missing value or quote). ERROR harnesses.local.toml:2: `claude` must be a table, e.g. [claude] Write [claude] on its own line, then enabled = false under it. ERROR harnesses.local.toml:3: [codex] `enabled` must be true or false Use true or false without quotes. Paths and ref must be quoted strings. WARN harnesses.local.toml:2: unknown key `enabeld` in [claude] A typo: the key is ignored until you fix it. WARN harnesses.local.toml:4: unknown harness [cursr] A typo, or a harness harnesses.toml doesn't list. It still loads.

Errors stop the command before it writes anything; warnings don't.

docs.title: Pack errors
docs.text:
Message Fix pack name `acme` is used by both [work] and [acme] Two packs share one name. Change name in one pack.toml, or set enabled = false for one in packs.local.toml. core is taken. skill `acme-deploy` is defined in both acme and acme2 Rename one. Each pack's items carry its own prefix. acme:skills/x: pack skills must start with `acme-` Rename the item to start with the pack's prefix. acme:pack.toml: `prefix` must be ASCII lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, ending with '-' Fix prefix in pack.toml, e.g. acme-. acme:pack.toml: `prefix` `aws-` uses the vendor name `aws`, ... reserved for official packs, ... one or two edits from the official name `brainrc` Rename the pack or its prefix to follow the naming rules. acme:pack.toml: requires_core `>=2.0` is not satisfied by core 1.2.3 Update core (git pull) or the pack, or set enabled = false for it in packs.local.toml. pack acme: no pack.toml at ... Fix the pack's path in packs.local.toml.

validate reports all of these. apply and status check each pack the same way first and write nothing while any of them stands, naming validate --pack <dir> for the pack to fix. See packs.md.

docs.title: Settings backups
docs.text:
Before apply changes a harness's settings file (Claude Code: ~/.claude/settings.json), it copies it next to the original as settings.json.bak-brainrc-<UTC time>. The last 5 are kept, counting old settings.json.bak-aicfg-<UTC time> backups too. No backup is made when the file didn't exist yet. MCP config files (~/.claude.json and the others) are backed up the same way.

The rewritten file and its backup keep the original's permissions, so a 0600 ~/.claude.json stays 0600. If the path is a symlink (a dotfiles-managed settings.json), apply writes through to the link's target and leaves the link in place; the backup goes next to the target.

docs.title: Apply while something else writes
docs.text:
Close Claude Code before apply changes MCP servers: it rewrites ~/.claude.json while it runs.

Message Fix ERROR another brainrc apply is running (lock: <path>) Another apply (or update) holds $BRAINRC_HOME/apply.lock. Let it finish, then re-run. The lock is released when that process exits, even if it crashed, so there is nothing to delete. CHANGED <harness> <file> (changed during apply; close Claude Code and re-run) The file changed after apply read it, so apply left it alone and exited 1. Close the harness that writes it, then re-run.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text:
python3 scripts/brainrc.py uninstall --dry-run   # see what goes
python3 scripts/brainrc.py uninstall             # or `brainrc uninstall` from the package

uninstall removes every link brainrc made (broken ones too), takes its hooks out of each settings file and the MCP servers it added out of each MCP file, and removes the files and directories that leaves empty. Your own settings, hooks, and servers stay, every file it rewrites is backed up first (*.bak-brainrc-*), and an instructions file init moved aside is put back. It reads which harnesses and source roots apply used from $BRAINRC_HOME/harnesses.json, so it still works after you move or delete the checkout or a pack.

Your local config (harnesses.local.toml, packs.local.toml, rules/*.local.md) and fetched git packs stay in $BRAINRC_HOME; uninstall --purge deletes that directory too, unless it holds files brainrc didn't make (then it says which, and leaves them). Then delete the repo, or uv tool uninstall brainrc (pipx uninstall brainrc).

docs.title: Every tool call is blocked, or doctor says hook missing
docs.text:
In older installs, a hook whose script had gone (checkout moved or deleted, package removed, Python upgraded) exited 2, which Claude Code treats as a block on every tool call. Run apply to rewrite the hook commands: they now skip a missing script (Cursor's reply "allow"), so the harness keeps working. That also means the guard is off until it's fixed, so doctor checks each one:

Finding Fix <harness>: hook missing: <path> Run apply from the checkout or install you use now; it re-links the hooks dir. <harness>: hook <path> exits <n> on an empty payload Run python3 <path> and read the error (often a Python too old for the guard), then apply. <harness>: hook <path> timed out after <n>s Run it by hand to see where it hangs. <harness>: hook <path> can't run: python3 is not on PATH Install Python 3, or put python3 on the PATH the harness starts with.

docs.title: A guard hook blocked something safe, or missed something risky
docs.text: The Claude Code hooks match command patterns (guardrails.md), so both happen. Open an issue with the exact command or tool call, what the hook did, and what you expected. A fix comes with two tests in tests/test_hooks.py: the risky command, and a safe near-miss that must still pass (for example git push origin x asks, git log doesn't).

docs.title: Tutorial: your first pack and domain skill
docs.text:
In this tutorial you build a pack called myteam with one domain skill for Protocol Buffers, install it into your AI tools, and check that spec-agent will load it for .proto files. It takes about 15 minutes. You need Python 3.11+ and git.

A pack is a separate repo layered on top of brainrc, so you never edit core. If you haven't yet, skim the architecture overview first.

Run every command from the core checkout unless a step says otherwise. CI runs steps 1-5 of this page on every change (scripts/check_tutorial.py), so they stay accurate.

docs.title: 1. Clone core, install it, and check it
docs.text:
git clone <this-repo> ~/brainrc
cd ~/brainrc
python3 scripts/brainrc.py apply
python3 scripts/brainrc.py validate

apply fetches the default pack, Gatework, and installs core and Gatework into your AI tools. validate should then print a line starting with OK: that counts skills, agents, and commands.

docs.title: 2. Create the pack
docs.text:
A pack needs a pack.toml. The prefix keeps your names apart from core's, requires_core says which core versions you tested against (copy the range from core's VERSION), and the [[extensions.gatework.domains]] row tells spec-agent (in the default Gatework pack) which files load your skill.

mkdir -p ~/src/myteam-ai-pack/skills/myteam-protobuf
cat > ~/src/myteam-ai-pack/pack.toml <<'EOF'
name = "myteam"
prefix = "myteam-"
requires_core = ">=0.6, <0.9"

[[extensions.gatework.domains]]
files = "`*.proto`, `buf.yaml`"
skills = ["myteam-protobuf"]
EOF

docs.title: 3. Write the domain skill
docs.text:
Domain skills have four sections: how to validate offline, conventions, a review checklist, and what never to do without approval. The description is what makes an AI tool load it.

cat > ~/src/myteam-ai-pack/skills/myteam-protobuf/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: myteam-protobuf
description: Protocol Buffers schemas for myteam services. Validation, conventions, and a review checklist for *.proto and buf.yaml. Use when changing or reviewing protobuf files.
---

# myteam-protobuf

## Validate (offline)
~~~bash
buf lint
buf breaking --against '.git#branch=main'
~~~

## Conventions
- One package per directory, named after the service and version (`myteam.billing.v1`).
- Never reuse or renumber a field. Reserve removed numbers and names.

## Review checklist
- A field changed type or number: that breaks every existing client.
- New required semantics on an existing message: needs a new version.

## Never without approval
- Publishing generated code or pushing to a schema registry.
EOF

docs.title: 4. Validate the pack
docs.text:
python3 scripts/brainrc.py validate --pack ~/src/myteam-ai-pack

You should see OK: with (packs: gatework, myteam) at the end: core, the default pack it fetched in step 1, and yours. A common mistake is a skill without the prefix. validate then names it, for example myteam:skills/protobuf: pack skills must start with `myteam-`.

docs.title: 5. Enable and install it
docs.text:
Packs are enabled per machine in packs.local.toml, which git ignores. status is a dry run and apply writes.

cat > packs.local.toml <<'EOF'
[myteam]
path = "~/src/myteam-ai-pack"
EOF
python3 scripts/brainrc.py status
python3 scripts/brainrc.py apply
python3 scripts/brainrc.py status | grep 'Everything in sync.'

The first status lists CREATE lines, including one for myteam-protobuf in each harness's skills directory. After apply, status prints Everything in sync.

docs.title: 6. Check what your AI tools now see
docs.text:
ls ~/.claude/skills/myteam-protobuf
grep myteam ~/.config/brainrc/extensions.md
python3 scripts/brainrc.py tokens | grep myteam

You should see SKILL.md, a Domains row for `*.proto`, `buf.yaml` naming myteam-protobuf, and the skill's cost in tokens. spec-agent reads that Domains row at the start of every ticket, so a ticket touching a .proto file now loads your skill.

docs.title: 7. Put the pack under version control
docs.text:
cd ~/src/myteam-ai-pack
git init -q
git add .
git -c user.name=you -c user.email=you@example.com commit -qm "Add myteam pack"

Then validate it in the pack's own CI on every push, against the core version you pin (Validate a pack in its own CI):

- uses: actions/checkout@<sha>
- uses: brainrc/brainrc/.github/actions/validate-pack@<core tag>

docs.text:

  • docs/packs.md is the full pack reference.
  • To add a domain skill to Gatework for everyone instead, open a pull request on brainrc/gatework: the skill goes in skills/<stack>/ with a row in the Domains table of skills/brainrc-gatework/SKILL.md.
